title.narrative: Increased capacity of constituents to build a strong and resilient social and solidarity economy for decent work

description.narrative:
The International Labour Organization (ILO) is implementing a strategy and action plan (SAP) following the resolution on decent work and the social and solidarity economy (SSE) adopted by the International Labour Conference in June 2022. This SAP includes three primary objectives: improved understanding of realities and needs related to decent work and the SSE, increased capacity to promote decent work and the SSE, and enhanced coherence on decent work and the SSE.
The ILO’s efforts feature the development of a guide to SSE legislation that equips stakeholders with tools to formulate and review SSE legislation through a decent work approach. It is also rolling out the Manage.COOP training tool to help improve the governance and management of cooperatives. Additionally, the Practical Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Training for Cooperatives in Agriculture is being used to improve OSH practices in agriculture through cooperatives. The Think.CareCoop and Start.CareCoop training tools are being implemented to provide care services through cooperatives. Moreover, a women leadership in cooperatives training package is being developed.
The ILO is co-chairing and handling secretariat responsibilities for the UN Inter-Agency Task Force on SSE, which has adopted a strategic action plan to support the implementation of the United Nations General Assembly Resolution on promoting the SSE for sustainable development. The ILO is also establishing and providing secretariat services for two technical working groups on statistics: the first, in the Task Force, on measuring the SSE; the second, in the Committee for the Promotion and Advancement of Cooperatives (COPAC), on measuring the economic contribution of cooperatives.
The strategic partners in this initiative include governments, employers’ and workers’ organizations, SSE networks and representative bodies, international organizations, research, education and training institutions, and national statistical office.
